World Suicide Prevention Day Celebrated
Saturday, 20 September 2025
1308 Hits
The Department of Psychiatry celebrated World Suicide Prevention Day with this year’s theme, “Changing the Narrative on Suicide.” The department premises came alive with creativity, awareness, and participation from students, patients, and staff alike.
The celebration began with an essay competition for undergraduate students, where Ms. Akanksha Mohanty and Mr. Pratham Bhandari impressed with their thoughtful writings. A poster competition followed for nursing students, who conveyed powerful messages through their artistic and innovative posters. Ms. Durga, Ms. Minal, and Ms. Kalyani were declared winners. Adding colour and warmth, patients of the department created beautiful rangoli designs; Ms. Sushma and Ms. Jyoti were awarded for their heartfelt contributions.
A highlight of the day was a Marathi play by nursing students, which through engaging performances, emphasized the importance of breaking silence on mental health. The play left a strong impact on patients, caregivers, and staff present.
The prize winners of all competitions were felicitated by Head of Department of Psychiatry, Dr. Sally John; Associate Professor, Dr. Harshal Sathe; Assistant Matron, Ms. Mangala Thakare; and Ward Incharge, Ms. Anita Kadam. Their words inspired participants and underlined the importance of collective action in suicide prevention.
The celebration concluded with prize distribution, appreciation for every participant, and a vote of thanks by Clinical Psychologist Mr. Mahanta Vaidya.
Suicide Prevention Day was celebrated on the 10
th
of September by doing various activities. Residents and consultants conducted an OPD awareness drive for suicide prevention where the outpatient clinics across MGIMS were covered. The Team met all consultants and residents working in the clinic and discussed the importance of suicide prevention awareness and available helpline catering to the needy. A yellow ribbon, which symbolises suicide prevention was worn by all doctors and small pamphlets mentioning the theme of suicide prevention day and helpline numbers were presented to all the doctors. The Response to the awareness drive was overwhelming with all the clinicians agreeing to give their best efforts for the cause.
The program not only spread awareness but also created joy, inspiration, and a shared commitment to changing the narrative on suicide.
